review.summary: Phase 23's package-security chunk delivers real, independently verifiable offline qualification at the declared source 79f03235…. The recorded receipt (docs/reviews/phase-23-chunk-package-security-attempt-02.checks.json, mirrored byte-identically in header/timestamp by docs/checks/phase-23.json) contains all 71 derived phase-23 commands at exit_code 0, timeout false, source_unchanged true, including the full 468-test Python suite, 14 compiler/feature matrices across MSRV 1.89.0 and 1.99.0, native export probe execution over 3820 frozen capabilities on both compilers, a fresh RustSec audit (1338 advisories, 206 locked deps, vulnerabilities.found false, lockfileUnchanged true), a source-bound private-material receipt, and both clean-package wrapper runs. The clean-package path is the strongest part: scripts/check-management-package.py packages from a detached worktree whose fingerprint must equal the reviewed source before and after, then binds the receipt to schemaVersion 3, sourceSha256, toolchain, requireClean/effectiveDirty, the package script, wrapper and old-consumer manifest hashes, the retained archive bytes and complete member ledger, full src/examples inventory equality, per-file byte equality for every packaged source and legal notice, the locally resolved rustc host/version, the external consumer feature manifest, four unique consumer execution indices and a distinct frozen-probe index. tools/management_consumers.py pins the four published 0.2.2 consumers to the verified registry archive c908cad8… and the phase-20 release receipt and requires current bytes to equal published bytes, so old-consumer compatibility is proven with genuine published sources (hashes 89c81…, d22fa…, 2b746…, 7103682… all reappear in both package receipts). All five attempt-1 findings are closed: the consumer manifest now declares and selects red-team = ["scm-sdk/red-team"] (so the previously vacuous red_team_dataplane cfg body genuinely compiles — the empty stdout is inherent to that frozen example, which only asserts), final-report and review-time checkpoint-binding re-verification exist with three new negative tests, host/compiler identity is resolved locally, the archive prefix guard is reachable and unit-tested, and tools/test_phase_checkpoint.py is reformatted. The offline/live boundary holds: qualification.json reports liveVerified 0 / liveRecorded 0 across 448 operations with liveAcceptance unverified, verify_offline_live_boundary rejects any current live receipt, live_evidence.py and check-access-release.py are excluded with documented reasons, and management_consumers prints executionClaimed false. CI routes only the contracts subset at phase 23 alongside the 48-job Rust matrix, and test_ci/test_management_phases enforce non-substitutability, gate ordering and documented counts. Remaining issues are three lows: archive-internal command cwd is unbound in receipt verification, retainedArchive relative paths are unanchored, and PHASES.md's "no new preserve_order" requirement is satisfied in fact (serde_json features = ["raw_value"]) but is not enforced by any executed check. No blocker or high finding.

findings.description: verify_receipt proves the four required archive-internal commands ('test --lib --no-default-features', 'test --lib --all-features', 'check --examples --all-features', 'test --doc --all-features') and the four 'run --example <name> --all-features' invocations are present only by matching the command vector. Unlike the consumer and frozen-probe bindings (lines 103-118), their 'cwd' is never bound, so a receipt whose archive-internal commands were executed in the repository checkout rather than in the extracted archive directory would still verify. The actual run is correct (docs/checks/phase-23-package-1.89.0.json records cwd /tmp/scm-sdk-archive-fuz85cow/scm-sdk for those entries), so this is an evidence-integrity hardening gap, not a false claim.
findings.required_fix: Bind the cwd of every required and packaged-example check to the extracted archive root (for example require pathlib.Path(row['cwd']).name == 'scm-sdk' and that it differs from the repository root and the consumer directory), and add a tools/test_management_package.py case rejecting a receipt whose archive-internal command recorded a different working directory.

findings.description: archive = pathlib.Path(report['retainedArchive']) is used as given. A relative value would resolve against the verifying process's working directory instead of the repository root, unlike tools/check_phase.py:750-752 which anchors a relative retainedArchive to root. Current receipts record absolute paths, so verification is sound today, but the check is weaker than its sibling and could silently bind a different file when run from another directory.
findings.required_fix: Anchor the value the same way as tools/check_phase.py:750-752 (resolve relative paths against root) and require an absolute, non-symlinked regular file; add a test covering a relative retainedArchive value.

findings.description: The phase 23 required evidence 'no new preserve_order' is not enforced by any command in commands_for(23). I verified the fact independently (crates/scm-sdk/Cargo.toml:44 declares serde_json features = ["raw_value"], and the only repository occurrences of preserve_order are documentation text plus the unrelated pagination test name page_and_item_iteration_preserve_order_and_duplicate_rows), but docs/checks/phase-23-dependencies.json records no resolved-feature ledger (serde_json at line 931 lists only name/version/license/source/rustVersion), so neither a direct nor a transitive enablement of serde_json/preserve_order would be caught by a check. The requirement currently rests on reviewer inspection.
findings.required_fix: Record and assert resolved features in scripts/check-dependencies.py from 'cargo metadata --all-features' resolve nodes (requiring serde_json's resolved feature set to exclude preserve_order), or add an explicit assertion in tools/test_dependency_policy.py / tools/test_management_phases.py that the serde_json manifest feature set equals {"raw_value"} and that no workspace feature forwards preserve_order.

limitations: Read-only Read/Glob/Grep only, with Bash disabled: I could not recompute SHA256 values or re-execute any check. The declared reviewed-source hash 79f03235… and the checks-file hash 955bd2a9… are taken as given; I verified internal consistency instead (receipt sourceSha256 fields, consumer hashes appearing in both package receipts, checkpoint binding structure, lockfile hashes).
Pass/fail conclusions rest on the recorded invocations, exit codes and stdout/stderr in the check receipts plus the source-binding logic in the verifying scripts, not on fresh execution.

The retained clean archives live at untracked absolute paths under .local/package-worktrees/06954db…/.local/artifacts/; I did not read those bytes, so archive_sha256 23a152c1… and 7de5e2db… are supported only by the receipts' member ledgers and the source-equality checks in scripts/check-management-package.py.
I did not read any credential or tenant-registration file and inspected nothing outside this repository.

The compatibility-matrix chunk's artifacts (contracts/native-fixtures/red-team-management.json, crates/scm-sdk/src/models/red_team_management.rs, src/airs/red_team/targets.rs, schema_graph.json, the red_team_management test suites, tools/management_fixtures.py, tools/red_team_management_models.py) are outside this chunk's declared scope; I treated their passing checks as inputs rather than auditing their content.

Remote CI has not run for this source; local receipts do not establish terminal remote coverage, as docs/RELEASE.md:168-172 states. Phase 24 deliverables (release version selection beyond the current 0.2.2 workspace version, changelog migration guidance, live tenant qualification, publication) are intentionally absent and were not judged.

docs/checks/phase-23-private-material.json records headCommit cd6600c53… (one commit before HEAD 06954db…) while its sourceSha256 equals the reviewed working-tree fingerprint; check_receipt validates only the format of headCommit. The historical tenant-occurrence classification therefore used the older HEAD, which is conservative, but the receipt does not bind HEAD identity.

docs/checks/* files are excluded from the review fingerprint (tools/review_phase.py:15-16), which is what makes the worktree/main-repo fingerprint equality in the package wrapper valid; I relied on the provided git status snapshot for the claim that only docs/checks and docs/reviews paths are uncommitted.
